overall: The Board's executive session minutes and November 14, 2017 minutes lacked required detail, requiring amendment; the other allegations (procedure, purpose, notice, untimely minutes claim, withholding) were rejected or declined.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to take a required vote and state all executive session subjects before entering executive session on three 2016-2017 dates.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore credit the Board’s version of the facts and find that the required vote was taken.

allegations.summary: Open session minutes for three executive sessions (Sept 2016, Mar 2017, Aug 2017) omitted the chair's statement of purpose and the pre-session vote, so they were not sufficiently detailed.
allegations.key_passage: Because the minutes at issue did not include this required information, we find that they were not sufficiently detailed to satisfy the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board improperly invoked Purpose 3 (litigation strategy) for executive sessions because no litigation was ongoing at the time.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board’s discussions of litigation strategy were appropriate for executive session, we find no violation with respect to this allegation.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board's Nov. 14, 2017 meeting notice omitted his requested transfer station discussion topic.
allegations.key_passage: Because the chair did not anticipate discussing the complainant’s letter, it was not required to appear on the meeting notice, and we find no violation with respect to this allegation.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Nov. 14, 2017 minutes reduced a 45-minute discussion about the landfill closure to one sentence, lacking required detail.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Board failed to create sufficiently detailed minutes in this instance.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board consistently failed to include sufficient detail in minutes about construction change orders, citing Feb. 23, 2016 minutes.
allegations.key_passage: Because the present allegation was made more than thirty days after the minutes at issue were approved, we find that it is untimely and we decline to review it.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board improperly withheld executive session minutes and failed to periodically review them for release.
allegations.key_passage: we note that the Board may withhold the minutes for as long as the purposes for the executive sessions remain ongoing.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Amend the November 14, 2017 minutes to provide the missing detail within thirty days of receipt of the letter, and certify compliance to the Attorney General in writing.
